_about: The makeyourmindup 3-second carousel format, as rows. Every carousel content-engine makes is held to these as refusals that fail the run, never warnings. Source: the locked v5 Library's docs/ve/cards/library/CAROUSEL-FORMAT.md (written 26 Nov 2026 from Krish's competitor sheet and his instruction that day: carousels follow "a really easy-to-understand format that someone can swipe through in 3 seconds and understand but it's also visually stunning"), its TITLES.md (his cover-title shapes) and library.json (carousel_sets and the carousel-* slot limits). Read by scripts/carousel_format.py (the checker), scripts/carousel_check.py (every deck and every drawn carousel), scripts/carousel_layout.py (the drawn cards' count), scripts/carousel_make.py (the one make route), scripts/post-pack/idea_checks.py (code carousel_format on the board's carousel options and the Saturday card count), scripts/post-pack/week_plan.py and scripts/saturday_goodnews.py (the good-news items), scripts/post-pack/story_score.py (the carousel_format floor) and scripts/post-pack/piece_manifest.py (a carousel that fails is not approvable). When docs/ve/cards/library/library.json is on this checkout the checker reads its slot limits too and takes the stricter of the two; tests/carousel_format_test.py fails if the two disagree. Until then it uses these rows and says so. A number or a word changes here, never in code.

ruling.said: Tell the Content-engine story intelligence for makeyourmindup v5 session that it is to enforce carousel formatting.
ruling.and: Production sessions do not "just randomly go off piste": the format is a refusal floor, and a session is creative only above it.

absent_detail: {script} is not on this checkout. The v5 Library is on content-engine main (b0cf8943, merged by #984); this checkout predates it or lacks it. No other renderer makes a carousel: no Codex card, no Growth template, no hand-drawn stand-in. Update the checkout from main, then run again.

route.rule: Every carousel is made by make_piece.py --set <set> in the registry's set order, and its first slide comes from make_covers.py. carousel_make.py is the one route: it checks the deck, calls both by path, checks the drawn slides and writes the receipt. Any other carousel maker refuses.

sets_note: The registry's carousel_sets at b0cf8943, mirrored so the checker works before the Library lands. The inside slides are the set's inside list in order, repeated whole (a one-template list repeats), 3 to 5 of them. tests/carousel_format_test.py fails when library.json is on the checkout and these differ.

slides.why: 4 to 7 slides: the cover, 3 to 5 inside, the close (CAROUSEL-FORMAT.md section 3, Hard numbers).

set_slides_why: The piece carousel is 6 slides: cover, chart (slide 2 carries the answer on its own), document, why-3, why-1, close (CAROUSEL-FORMAT.md section 4; PRODUCTION-PLAYBOOK.md).

good_news.why: The good-news roundup defaults to 4 items: five break the 50-word ceiling (CAROUSEL-FORMAT.md worked example B), and the registry's good-news set holds four item templates. A weekly good news may find a fifth story as a spare; the carousel carries four.

type_floor_why: Nothing below 34 px anywhere at 1080 wide (CAROUSEL-FORMAT.md, Type, absolute floor).

cover.why: Cover headline 10 words or fewer and 50 characters or fewer, in one of his title shapes (TITLES.md), 120 px or more at 1080 wide; one dominant hero visual plus the wordmark.

inside.not_counted_why: The step counter, the source credit, the photo credit and the site do not count (CAROUSEL-FORMAT.md, Words, any inside slide in total).
inside.question_templates_why: Every inside slide is a statement, never a question. The one exception is the Library's own quiz set: its carousel-quiz-question template is the quiz's question, answered on the next slide by carousel-quiz-answer.
inside.why: One glance line of 8 words or fewer at 96 px or more; 15 words at most a slide; 50 across all inside slides; one dominant visual filling at least half the slide; every inside slide a statement.

slide_two.why: Instagram re-shows an unswiped carousel from slide 2, so slide 2 carries the answer on its own: it names the subject and never opens on "this", "it" or "as above" (CAROUSEL-FORMAT.md, The inside slides).

close.why: The close is the takeaway (44 characters or fewer, two lines, its payoff in mint), the S3h wordmark and the site. Never "Follow for more": the follow ask goes in the caption.

how_to.why: How-to: one step per slide, 5 at most, the real screenshot as the dominant visual, an overlay prompt of 5 words or fewer.

never.why: the close never asks to follow; the follow ask goes in the caption
no swipe cue in words; the picture breaking into slide 2 does that job
no exclamation marks in reader-facing text

library_slots._about: Which Library slot carries each role, by template, so the checker reads the slot's max_chars, max_lines and min_size_px when library.json is here, and the agreement test compares them with the rows above.

library_shrink_known._why: Found on 26 Nov 2026 when origin/main (the locked v5 Library, b0cf8943 via #984) was merged into story/engine-v5: these Library slots may shrink-to-fit below the format floor (96 px for a glance, 34 px for any text). The deck check holds every glance, headline and takeaway to its slot's max_chars and the format's word limits, so a slot rarely needs to shrink, and the floor stays the rule. Raising each slot's min_size_px in library.json is the Library's change, not this file's: it waits on Krish (the Library is locked). tests/carousel_format_test.py fails on any disagreement not listed here, and on a listed one that no longer holds, so the list only shrinks.
